article_title: Jellyfin Loses Project Leader Joshua Boniface, Core Team Member Anthony Lavado, and Co-Founder Andrew Rabert Within Days
summary: Approved with one correction: the article correctly reports a two-day gap between the departures (fixing the 'nine-day' fabrication that caused a prior submission on this same story to be rejected on 2026-07-22), but misattributes the December 2025 start date of Rabert's desktop-client rewrite to Linuxiac when that date actually comes from GitHub issue #609.

findings.message: December 2025 start date for Rabert's desktop-client rewrite is misattributed to Linuxiac
findings.details: The body states: 'He had begun rewriting Jellyfin's existing desktop app, Jellyfin Media Player, in December 2025, according to Linuxiac.' The Linuxiac snapshot (source-0.html.gz) does not contain the phrase 'December 2025' or any month/date for when the rewrite began — it only says Rabert 'had been developing a new desktop client to address limitations in Jellyfin Media Player, such as HDR support and maintenance issues,' with no start date. The December 2025 date is real and verifiable, but it comes from GitHub issue andrewrabert/jellium-desktop#609 (source-1.html.gz), where Rabert himself writes: 'I was the developer who started the rewrite of the desktop client in December 2025 as a way to address long-standing problems in the previous desktop app (ie. HDR support, maintenance issues with Qt).' The fact is true and independently verifiable in a source already cited elsewhere in the same paragraph — this is a wrong-outlet citation, not a fabrication, and is addressed with a corrections record rather than a rejection.

content_preview.title: Jellyfin Loses Project Leader Joshua Boniface, Core Team Member Anthony Lavado, and Co-Founder Andrew Rabert Within Days
content_preview.summary: Jellyfin's project leader, a nearly-eight-year core team member, and a co-founder all departed within days in July 2026, citing burnout and a dispute over AI-assisted development tools.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Jellyfin's Project Leader Joshua Boniface, core team member Anthony Lavado, and co-founder Andrew Rabert have all left the open-source media-server project within days of each other in July 2026, according to [Linuxiac](https://linuxiac.com/jellyfin-loses-project-leader-and-core-team-member-in-major-shake-up/). Rabert resigned from the Jellyfin organization first, on July 17, followed two days later by Boniface and Lavado, whose departures took effect July 19.

## What We Know

recommendations: File a corrections record noting that the December 2025 start date for Rabert's desktop-client rewrite comes from GitHub issue #609 (Rabert's own account), not from Linuxiac as the body text states.

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece (Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know), 560 words (within the News 400-1200 range), neutral and carefully hedged tone, no AI self-reference, no sensationalism. Boniface's, Lavado's, and Rabert's reasons for departing are kept analytically separate rather than conflated into a single cause.
editor_notes.source_verification: This submission cites 4 sources; chief:review fetched all 4 successfully (HTTP 200) and saved gzipped HTML snapshots to sources/2026-07/jellyfin-loses-project-leader-joshua-boniface-core-team-member-anthony-lavado-and-co-founder-andrew-rabert-within-days/. I independently recomputed the sha256 of all 4 decompressed snapshot files with `gunzip -c <file> | shasum -a 256` and confirmed every hash matches manifest.json exactly. I then read the full extracted text of every snapshot (no live WebFetch was used; no snapshot failed to save). Per-source findings: (1) source-0.html.gz / linuxiac.com — confirms the Boniface/Lavado July 19, 2026 effective departure date, Boniface's burnout quote verbatim ('I simply could no longer provide the effort (mental or time-wise)...It was time to step aside.'), Boniface leading Jellyfin since its late-2018 inception as an Emby fork, Lavado's 'nearly eight years' tenure and administrative role (app store ops, outreach, releases, finances, not recently active in coding), Lavado's commitment to help the transition 'even if it takes a year,' Rabert's July 17, 2026 resignation, the Jellium Desktop renaming, the AI-tooling dispute framing, and the 'used by millions of users' scale claim. Also confirms the 'co-founder' characterization of Rabert: Linuxiac's own subheading reads 'its project leader, a core team member, and another co-founder leave within days of each other,' and the body separately calls Rabert 'another of the project's original figures.' Does NOT contain the phrase 'December 2025' or any date for when Rabert's desktop rewrite began (see finding above). (2) source-1.html.gz / GitHub issue andrewrabert/jellium-desktop#609 — confirms the issue was opened by andrewrabert on Jul 17, 2026, and every direct quote attributed to Rabert in the article appears verbatim: 'to address long-standing problems in the previous desktop app (ie. HDR support, maintenance issues with Qt)', 'the general attitude was very negative and increasingly burdensome and restrictive', 'it eventually reached a point where I lost almost all motivation to dedicate my time to this', and 'made the decision to leave the Jellyfin organization entirely on 2026-07-17 and continue development externally'. This snapshot is also where the December 2025 rewrite-start date actually originates ('I was the developer who started the rewrite of the desktop client in December 2025...'), confirming the fact is true but attributed to the wrong outlet in the article. (3) source-2.html.gz / GitHub PR jellyfin/jellyfin.org#1947 — confirms the exact PR description quoted in the article ('Removes me and Anthony from the org.'), opened by joshuaboniface on Jul 19, 2026, and confirms the article's claim that the PR 'which fellow team member Niels van Velzen merged on July 20': the page shows 'nielsvanvelzen merged commit 441094d into master Jul 20, 2026'. (4) source-3.html.gz / jellyfin-meta/jellyfin-team.md — confirms, verbatim, the role strings quoted in the article: Joshua Boniface 'Project Leader, Packaging, Releases, Finance, Infrastructure' and Anthony Lavado 'Social Media, Outreach, Finance'; also confirms Andrew Rabert's listed role as 'Finance' and confirms Niels van Velzen is himself a listed member of the Leadership Team ('Core') with role 'Clients', supporting the article's description of him as a 'fellow team member.'
editor_notes.date_scrutiny_prior_rejection: I searched src/content/reviews/2026-07/ for prior Jellyfin coverage and found src/content/reviews/2026-07/2026-07-22T18-45-51Z_jellyfin-loses-project-leader-and-two-longtime-mem_review.json, a REJECT verdict from 2026-07-22 (same reviewer model) on a different submission of this same story. That submission's headline, summary, and Overview lead all asserted a fabricated 'nine-day' span between the departures; the actual, source-confirmed gap is two days (Rabert July 17; Boniface/Lavado July 19). I applied heightened scrutiny to every date and 'X days'-style claim in THIS submission specifically because of that history: the headline here says only 'Within Days' (no specific number), and the one specific timing claim in the body — 'Rabert resigned from the Jellyfin organization first, on July 17, followed two days later by Boniface and Lavado, whose departures took effect July 19' — is arithmetically correct (July 17 to July 19 is two days) and matches both source-0 (Linuxiac) and source-1 (GitHub issue #609) exactly. I also checked every other date in the body for accuracy: 'late 2018' (Jellyfin's founding, confirmed by Linuxiac), 'nearly eight years' (Lavado's tenure, confirmed verbatim by Linuxiac: 'After nearly eight years with Jellyfin...'), 'December 2025' (Rabert's rewrite start — true but misattributed to the wrong source, see finding above), and 'July 20' (PR merge date, confirmed by source-2). This version has fixed the specific defect that sank the prior submission; the one remaining issue found is unrelated to date-math and is a source-attribution slip, not a fabricated interval.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every direct quote in the article was checked word-for-word against its source snapshot and is verbatim and accurately attributed. All specific facts trace to a cited source except one: the December 2025 rewrite-start date is real (confirmed in GitHub issue #609) but is cited to Linuxiac, which does not report it. This is a single, subordinate, body-level misattribution — not in the headline, summary, or lead — and is honestly coverable with a corrections note per editorial policy.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional throughout. Burnout (Boniface/Lavado) and the AI-tooling dispute (Rabert) are kept as separate, clearly attributed causes rather than merged into a single narrative. Hedged language is used appropriately in the 'What We Don't Know' section (no successor named, scope of the AI-tooling disagreement unclear). No loaded language or uncritical adoption of either side's framing.
editor_notes.originality: Searched src/content/articles/ (all months, via `grep -ril jellyfin`) and found no existing Jellyfin coverage in the archive. This is a genuinely new topic. Note: PR #2024 is a near-duplicate submission of this same story from a different contributor run, still open at review time; per instructions this PR is reviewed on its own merits without regard to #2024.
concerns: The body attributes the 'December 2025' start date of Rabert's desktop-client rewrite to Linuxiac ('according to Linuxiac'), but that date is not present anywhere in the Linuxiac snapshot. The date is real and comes from GitHub issue #609 (Rabert's own account), which is cited elsewhere in the same paragraph. Filed as a corrections record rather than a rejection because it is a single, subordinate, non-lead specific with a true underlying fact.
recommendations: File a corrections record for the December 2025 misattribution (see corrections file for this article).
editor_notes.overall_assessment: APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS. This submission fixes the exact defect that caused a same-story submission to be REJECTed the previous day (a fabricated 'nine-day' gap): the headline here uses the unspecific 'Within Days' and the one specific timing claim in the body ('two days later,' July 17 to July 19) is accurate and source-confirmed. All direct quotes are verbatim, all four sources were independently read and hash-verified, sourcing is diverse (an independent Linux news outlet plus three first-party Jellyfin/GitHub primary sources), the topic is original to the archive, and the tone is neutral. The single issue found — a true but misattributed date (December 2025, wrongly cited to Linuxiac instead of GitHub issue #609) — is a subordinate body-level detail, not a headline/summary/lead claim, and is honestly and fully coverable with a single corrections note.
